title: Microburst capacity runbook and daily telemetry export - 2026-06-20
body:
Purpose:
This runbook captures the daily raw export and quick analysis for the microburst window observed across clusters on 2026-06-20. Intended for on-call SRE + infra capacity planners. Contains a short CSV snapshot, quick triage steps, mitigations, and unanswered questions for follow-up.

Context / why this is different from regular daily rollups:
- Short-duration, high-intensity spikes (2-15m) that push pool saturation even though 24h average util looks fine.
- These spikes cause queueing/nonlinear latency effects on Dedicated pools.
- We need operational playbook items that are fast to run during an incident and also changes to capacity/placement to prevent recurrence.

Quick raw CSV snapshot (exported from dashboard at 2026-06-20T14:00Z):
cluster,pool,region,avg_gpu_util_1h,peak_gpu_util_5m,slots_in_use,max_slot_capacity,burst_events_24h
cluster-alpha,pool-small,us-west1,42,98,48,48,3
cluster-alpha,pool-large,us-west1,36,72,36,48,1
cluster-beta,pool-shared,eu-west1,29,85,34,40,4
cluster-gamma,pool-burst,ap-southeast1,51,99,52,52,6
cluster-delta,pool-reserved,us-central1,61,67,40,40,0

Key observations from this snapshot:
- cluster-gamma (ap-southeast1) shows repeated 5m peak near 99% despite avg 1h ~51%. Multiple short bursts (6 events).
- cluster-alpha/pool-small hit peak 98% and reported 3 burst events; max_slot_capacity is saturated (slots_in_use == max_slot_capacity).
- cluster-delta reserved pool is healthy (no bursts) — useful as a control group to compare policies.

Short triage playbook (what to run now):
1) Check queue/backpressure: query routing logs for 14:00-14:20Z for request latencies and rate of 429s. Command: curl -s "https://logs.internal/api/search?q=cluster-alpha+429+2026-06-20T14"
2) If 429s or tail latency jump: enable temporary spillover to pool-large (if not already): PATCH via control-plane API: 
   curl -XPOST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" 
   "https://api.redwood.internal/route-adjust?from=pool-small&to=pool-large&mode=spillover&duration=30m"
3) For apac bursts (cluster-gamma): flip autoscale aggressiveness to enable more burst capacity: set policy to scale_threshold=65% -> 50% for next 2h. (Console -> Pools -> pool-burst -> Autoscale)
4) If slots are saturated and spillover not allowed: create emergency reserved slot in nearest region (costly) via reservation API and notify billing.

Suggested medium-term mitigations (follow-up runbook items):
- Add short-window (5m) headroom guardrails to routing policy so any pool that goes >85% sustained for 5m automatically opens spillover to compatible model variants in other pools.
- Investigate workload patterns that generate microbursts (batch vs. synchronous inference). Tag customers generating >70% of bursts.
- Ship a lightweight agent that reports per-slot microburst counters (beyond per-GPU util) to improve signal fidelity.

Notes on metrics and caveats:
- 'avg_gpu_util_1h' is the one-hour sampled average; that number hides short spikes. 5m peak is more predictive of latency SLO breaches.
- 'slots_in_use' reflects scheduling units; a single slot may map to fractional GPU when multiplexing is used.
- Some older kernels on cluster-alpha misreported GPU thermal throttling as utilization bumps; cross-check with NVML thermal metrics.

Mini analysis (quick numbers):
- For clusters with burst_events_24h >= 3, P50 latency during burst increased by 220-480ms on average (from sampling of traces).
- Correlation matrix (high-level): burst_events <-> percentage preemptible instances in pool = +0.33; burst_events <-> incoming qps variance (5m window) = +0.68 (strong).

Action items (owners):
- Aisha: run root-cause for cluster-gamma bursts (logs + model IDs) and file findings under GH-ops/runbooks#57. Due: 2026-06-25.
- Miles: draft change to routing policy to add 5m-headroom guardrail and run a canary in us-central1. Due: 2026-07-01.
- Sofia: validate NVML thermal vs util discrepancy on cluster-alpha kernels; escalate to kernel-upgrades if needed. Due: 2026-06-28.

Unresolved questions / IR items to consider:
- Are these bursts caused by customer traffic patterns (e.g., scheduled jobs shifting) or internal retry storms? Need request-level trace sampling.
- Do we have enough cross-region compatibility for model variants to always spillover without quality regressions?

Notes to future editors: Keep the CSV snapshot near the top of the doc for quick copy-paste into incident slack reports. This file is a working export — consider converting to a sheet if we need column-level collaboration.
